title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: An economic system of private ownership of the means of production, run for profit in free markets.
A political force rooted in a shared regional and cultural identity (custom, language, religion); loyalty to one's nation.
The late 19th-century drive of strong states for colonies and spheres of influence.

en.text: Capitalism, fully fledged in Britain and the Netherlands by the 16th–17th centuries, became industrial in the Industrial Revolution (Britain, about 1750 or 1780 to 1850), with deep economic, social and political results that ended in late 19th-century imperialism. Nationalism, the strongest political force from the 1850s, drove the unification of Italy (led by Piedmont) and Germany (led by Prussia under Bismarck), and the Eastern Question in the Balkans. In the USA, slavery led to secession and the Civil War of 1861–1865, which ended both.

am.text: ካፒታሊዝም ወደ ኢንዱስትሪ አብዮት አደገ፤ ብሔርተኝነት ጣሊያንንና ጀርመንን አዋሐደ፤ ባርነት የአሜሪካን የእርስ በርስ ጦርነት አስነሳ፤ የምሥራቁ ጥያቄ ወደ ባልካን ጦርነቶች አመራ።

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Capitalism: private ownership, two antagonistic classes, profit, laissez-faire.
Industrial Revolution: Britain, about 1750 (or 1780) to 1850; factories and steam.
Its results led to late 19th-century imperialism.
Nationalism: the most powerful force in the West from the 1850s.
Germany was united under Prussia by Bismarck's three wars (1864–1871).
USA: slavery caused secession; the North's victory (1861–1865) ended both.
Eastern Question: the fate of the declining Ottoman Empire.
The Balkan Wars (1912–1913) took almost all of the Ottomans' European lands.

Italy was the first industrial country

notes.text: Review I Q5 (president of the Confederacy) cannot be answered from the unit text, which never names Jefferson Davis; the item is kept with the answer in its explanation. Consider replacing it with "The President of the USA during the Civil War was ___ (Abraham Lincoln)".

Unit Summary: Industrial Revolution "1851" (lesson text 1850); Eastern Question "since the 1850s" (lesson: late 18th–early 20th c.); Balkan Wars took "all" Ottoman European land (lesson: except eastern Thrace and Adrianople). The lessons follow the lesson text.
The Adwa challenge is an added Ethiopian link. Review II items are turned into choose/sort items; the KEY exam book has no history papers here, so the chapter test draws from the section tests.
